history.dynasty: Maratha period (managed today by the Devotees' Mandal under the West Maharashtra Devasthan Committee)
history.period: Original shrine tradition 500-600 years; Nrusinha Saraswati (1378-1458) resided here 12 years
history.summary: Narsobawadi (Narsobachi Wadi) is one of the principal Datta Kshetras of Maharashtra, situated at the confluence of the Krishna and Panchganga rivers in Shirol taluka, Kolhapur district. Shri Nrusinha Saraswati, the second incarnation of Lord Dattatreya, lived here for 12 years (per the Shri Guru Charitra) after completing Chaturmas at Audumbar, leaving his nirgun padukas (holy sandals) under an audumbara tree for worship — there is no idol of the deity, only the padukas. The shrine is at nearby Pancha Ganga Sagar, where the five tributaries Shiva, Bhadra, Kumbhi, Bhagwati and Saraswati merge into the Krishna. The place was sanctified further by saints including Vasudevananda Saraswati (Tembe Swami), who stayed here 12 years; his room is near the temple. Saint Eknath is said to have got the ghat built, and the Adilshahi ruler Adilshah was a devotee who donated lands. The original mandir on the Krishna-Panchganga confluence carries a tradition of 500-600 years. Nearby are the Datta Amareshwar Temple and the Yakshini/Shakti teertha. Daily routine: Kakad Aarti and Paduka Puja at 5:00 AM, Rudrabhishek 8:00 AM-12:00 noon, Maha Puja and Aarti 12:30-1:30 PM, Pavamana Sookta Parayan 3:00-4:00 PM, Dhoop Aarti 7:30 PM, Palkhi at 8:00 PM and Shej Aarti at 10:00 PM. Large fairs are held on Purnima days and during Kanyagat. The CSV town 'Kolhapur' is the district; the actual village is Narsobawadi, ~48 km from Kolhapur city and ~19-22 km from Sangli.

name: Narsobawadi Temple (Shri Nrusinha Saraswati Datta Mandir)
town_description: Narsobawadi (Nrusinhwadi, Narsobachi Wadi) is a village and major Datta Kshetra in Shirol taluka, Kolhapur district, Maharashtra, at the confluence of the Krishna and Panchganga rivers, about 48 km from Kolhapur city and about 19-22 km from Sangli.

travel.road: Narsobawadi is reachable by road from Kolhapur (~48 km) and Sangli (~20 km); local transport available from both cities

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Dattatreya Jayanti (Margashirsha Purnima) and Guru Purnima are the biggest festivals
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily approximately 5:00 AM-10:00 PM (Kakad Aarti 5:00 AM; Palkhi 8:00 PM; Shej Aarti 10:00 PM, after which the temple closes)
